ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, Vo is the middle common node, connected to the drain terminal of M1 below and to the lower terminals of the upper load transistors M2 and M3. The source terminal of M1 is grounded, and the gate is driven by Vin. M3 is located on the upper left; its upper terminal is connected to VDD, and its gate is controlled by the DC bias VG. M2 is located on the upper right, connected between VDD and Vo, and its control terminal is connected to a VDD-related node; under small signal, VDD is AC ground, and VG is also AC ground. Reasoning: Since λ ≠ 0, each transistor has a finite output resistance ro. In the small-signal equivalent, M1 provides ro1 from the output node to ground, while its transconductance produces a current gm1·Vin from drain to source, causing the output voltage to decrease as Vin increases. The source and gate of M3 are at AC ground, so looking in from Vo, it mainly contributes ro3 to AC ground. The upper terminal/control terminal of M2 is at AC ground, so the small-signal equivalent resistance looking in from Vo is 1/gm2 in parallel with ro2. Therefore the total resistance at the output node is Rout = ro1 ∥ ro3 ∥ (1/gm2 ∥ ro2). Therefore the voltage gain is Vo/Vin = -gm1·Rout.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, the channel length modulation of all transistors is non-zero (\(\lambda \neq 0\)). Also, all transistors operate in saturation and have negligible body effect. The AC small signal voltage gain \(V_o/V_{in}\) of the circuit is ______.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology: Vo is the common node between the drain of M1 and the upper load transistors M2 and M3; M1 source is grounded and its gate is driven by Vin; M2 is diode-connected to the AC-ground VDD rail; M3 has gate biased by VG and source at VDD. In small signal, set VDD and VG to AC ground. Looking into Vo, M1 contributes ro1 to ground, M3 contributes ro3 to ground, and diode-connected M2 contributes (1/gm2 || ro2) to ground. Therefore the total output resistance is Rout = ro1 || ro3 || (1/gm2 || ro2). The M1 transconductance current is gm1 Vin from drain to source, so Vo/Vin = -gm1 Rout = -gm1(ro1 || (1/gm2 || ro2) || ro3).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中 Vo 是中间公共节点，连接到下方 M1 的漏端以及上方负载管 M2、M3 的下端。M1 的源端接地，栅极由 Vin 驱动。M3 位于上方左侧，其上端接 VDD，栅极由直流偏置 VG 控制。M2 位于上方右侧，接在 VDD 与 Vo 之间，其控制端接到 VDD 相关节点；小信号下 VDD 为交流地，VG 也为交流地。
推理：由于 λ ≠ 0，各管都有有限输出电阻 ro。小信号等效中，M1 在输出节点提供 ro1 到地，同时其跨导产生从漏到源的电流 gm1·Vin，使输出电压随 Vin 增大而下降。M3 的源和栅在交流地，因此从 Vo 看进去主要贡献 ro3 到交流地。M2 的上端/控制端在交流地，从 Vo 看进去的小信号等效电阻为 1/gm2 与 ro2 并联。因此输出节点总电阻为 Rout = ro1 ∥ ro3 ∥ (1/gm2 ∥ ro2)。所以电压增益为 Vo/Vin = -gm1·Rout。

planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text conditions that lambda is nonzero, so ro terms must be retained; all devices are in saturation, so saturation small-signal gm/ro models apply; body effect is negligible, so no gmb terms are included.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the MOSFET small-signal model in saturation with nonzero channel-length modulation: each transistor has ro. DC voltage sources VDD and VG become AC ground. A diode-connected MOS presents approximately 1/gm in parallel with ro. A transistor whose gate and source are both at AC ground contributes only ro to the output node. A common-source input transistor produces an output current gm1*vin, giving a negative voltage gain equal to minus gm1 times the total resistance seen at the drain.

method.method_draft: After describing the image topology, write KCL directly at the output node Vo in the small-signal circuit. Since VDD and VG are AC ground, the admittances from Vo to ground are gds1 from M1, gds3 from M3, and for diode-connected M2 the admittance gm2 + gds2. The input-controlled current of M1 contributes gm1*Vin leaving the output node for a positive Vin, causing an inverted output. Thus KCL gives (gds1 + gds3 + gds2 + gm2)Vo + gm1 Vin = 0. Hence Vo/Vin = -gm1/(gds1 + gds3 + gds2 + gm2). Replacing gds_i by 1/ro_i and rewriting 1/(gm2+gds2) as (1/gm2 || ro2), obtain Vo/Vin = -gm1(ro1 || ro3 || (1/gm2 || ro2)).
